title: The Last Ghost Anew
premise: Ulyana Joubert, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent five years laundering her own past as carefully as she audits others' money, discovers that Flight 4471 — a plane still in the air — has been erased from every database she can touch. The vanished flight is a shell company made of people: a billionaire's death-faking scheme that Ulyana's own estranged mentor helped design. As the conspirators close in on the one person whose records they missed, Ulyana must decide whether to trade her buried secret — her true identity and the crime she committed to become 'Ulyana' — for the leverage to expose them. In the end she burns her old self deliberately, testifies under her real name, and walks out of the courthouse into a life with no clean money left to hide behind.
about_author: A. M. Pemberton is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade inside the quiet machinery of international finance before leaving to write about the people it erases. They live in Lisbon, where they claim the best view of any airport in Europe.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. Ulyana closes another routine case at the Financial Integrity Unit, showing her meticulous, rule-bound world and the exhaustion beneath it. A colleague jokes that she's the only investigator with no vices — no history anyone can find. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being perfectly unremarkable.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. An automated flag pings: a private flight from Geneva has no departure record, no manifest, no tail number — yet radar shows it airborne right now. Her supervisor tells her to drop it; the system doesn't make mistakes like this. Emotional beat: the first crack of obsession.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Boarded
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. She traces the jet's ownership through six shells to Aurel Vassek, a shipping magnate officially dead for two years. Someone has already wiped his death certificate too. Emotional beat: vertigo — the records are being rewritten faster than she reads them.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. New compliance directives arrive overnight forbidding exactly the queries she's been running. Her access quietly narrows. She realizes someone inside the Unit is watching her watch them. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Marta
chapters.summary: POV: Marta Okonkwo, Ulyana's oldest friend and a disgraced air-traffic controller. Marta confirms 4471 landed at a decommissioned strip in Sardinia — and that she was paid to forget it. She warns Ulyana to stop. Emotional beat: loyalty offered and refused.

chapters.title: Five Years of Nobody
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana (flashback-threaded). We learn how 'Ulyana Joubert' was constructed after a catastrophe in her old life — a name bought, a history laundered like money. The chapter reveals she knows exactly how identities get erased because she erased herself. Emotional beat: dread of exposure.

chapters.title: The Auditor Comes Calling
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. A charming internal auditor, Deshawn Reyes, appears to review her caseload — and asks oddly precise questions about her pre-Unit employment. He knows there's a gap. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she's also prey.

chapters.title: Sardinia
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. Using leave she shouldn't take, Ulyana reaches the abandoned airstrip and finds the hangar converted into a data center — servers humming, guarded, feeding something. She photographs everything. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into fear when she spots surveillance cameras recording her.

chapters.title: What Vassek Bought
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Ulyana/Marta. The photos reveal the scheme: Vassek didn't fake his death alone — he sold 'erasure' as a service to a dozen elites, using live flights as moving vaults of deleted records. Emotional beat: scale dawning; this is an industry.

chapters.title: The Mentor
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. She confronts Ilya Brandt, her former teacher and the architect of the very laundering methods she once used — now Vassek's designer. He offers her partnership and protection if she walks away. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Marta Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. Marta stops answering calls; her apartment is stripped clean. Either she ran or was taken. Ulyana finds one clue taped inside Marta's old headset: a server address. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Deshawn's Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Deshawn. Revealed as Vassek's fixer inside the Unit, he gives Ulyana a choice: hand over her evidence and her own fabricated identity will stay sealed, or lose everything. He shows he already has her real birth name. Emotional beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Secret Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. Alone, she weighs her options: her hidden identity is now the only currency Vassek's network truly fears — proof that their erasure service has a flaw, a woman who slipped through. Emotional beat: turning point from hiding to bargaining.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Leverage
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. She feeds Deshawn partial truths, buying time while she and a recontacted, terrified Marta map the network's command structure. Emotional beat: the thrill and guilt of becoming a manipulator herself.

chapters.title: Flight 4472
chapters.summary: POV: multiple. A second ghost flight launches carrying the network's master ledger — physical, offline, untouchable. Vassek intends to retire the whole operation mid-air. Ulyana realizes the ledger is her only path to real proof. Emotional beat: clock starting.

chapters.title: Brandt's Confession
chapters.summary: POV: Brandt. Dying of illness, Brandt meets Ulyana and admits he built the system to protect clients but stayed to protect himself — and that he taught her everything because she reminded him of who he'd failed to be. He gives her the boarding protocol. Emotional beat: forgiveness neither asked for.

chapters.title: Boarding Pass
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. Using Brandt's protocol, Ulyana gets herself listed on 4472 as cargo escort — a person the system must acknowledge even as it deletes everyone else. Emotional beat: stepping willingly into the machine that erases people.

chapters.title: Thirty Thousand Feet
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. Mid-flight, she copies the ledger while Vassek — alive, urbane, ruthless — works three seats away, unaware. Deshawn, aboard as security, recognizes her. Emotional beat: sustained terror; nowhere to run at altitude.

chapters.title: The Erasure
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. Deshawn corners her over the Atlantic; Vassek orders the plane itself flagged for deletion — a tomb in the sky. Ulyana triggers an emergency transponder broadcast of the ledger fragments, making the flight famous enough to never vanish. Emotional beat: sacrifice of invisibility as survival.

chapters.title: Landing
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. Forced down in Marseille by the broadcast storm, Ulyana is detained — but so are Vassek and Deshawn, as journalists and prosecutors descend on a flight that officially never existed. Emotional beat: chaos as liberation.

chapters.title: Her Real Name
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. To testify, she surrenders the last thing she owns: the secret of who she was before. Under oath she speaks her birth name and the crime that forced her to bury it. Emotional beat: identity chosen rather than hidden.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: POV: Ulyana. Months later, the network is dismantled, Marta is found and rebuilding, and Ulyana — unemployed, unhidden, finally ordinary — watches planes land in Lisbon without flinching. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; being seen is not the same as being caught.
